title: Even–Mansour Security for Reset-Secure Sources
summary: Even–Mansour pseudorandom-permutation security is known for computationally unpredictable sources, while the extension to reset-secure sources remains conjectural.

formal_statement.body: In the random-permutation model, the Even–Mansour construction has a pseudorandom-permutation security theorem for computationally unpredictable sources. The unresolved task is to prove the corresponding pseudorandom-permutation theorem when the source is computationally reset-secure, a conjectured extension whose proof appears nontrivial; establishing it would validate the assumption used for the seeded sponge application.

scope.domain: Public-seed pseudorandom permutations based on the Even–Mansour construction in the random-permutation model.
assumptions: The analysis is in the random-permutation model.
The target source is computationally reset-secure.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the corresponding Even–Mansour pseudorandom-permutation security theorem for computationally reset-secure sources.

progress.summary: The paper explicitly conjectures extending its Even–Mansour theorem from computationally unpredictable sources to computationally reset-secure sources. It says the statement evades a simple proof and would validate the seeded-sponge assumption.
citation_labels: Pratik Soni et al., Public-Seed Pseudorandom Permutations
